incidents.name: TrustedVolumes
incidents.notes: RFQ proxy had permissionless registerAllowedOrderSigner and checked authorization against order.taker (attacker) instead of order.maker, draining the maker's approved balances.

sources.ref: delegatecall-target review (callTracer + prestateTracer on the exploit tx, then eth_getStorageAt over [creation block, incident block]): the victim holds no EIP-1967 slot and no low storage slot - it is a selector-to-module router. The exploit tx DELEGATECALLs 0xeeeeee53...1756 -> 0x88eb28009351fb414a5746f5d8ca91cdc02760d8 twice (selectors 0xea7faa61 and 0x4112e1c2), and prestateTracer shows that address read from the keccak slots 0x5955181dc8ce5ace66c1381b7c1d9e383dc48785bde6e1b360d80ddb0ed66fe5 and 0x7b810de52829a346e3111da05d9f909e0b9f42c113f6778a31f5262c8f9d2ba9. Binary-searching both between the creation block 20572034 and the incident block 25039670 gives the same two-step history: installed as 0x626784d4af1e8d37b13b42f5fd2c9959c1711952 on 2024-08-20 (blocks 20572604 / 20572606, hours after deployment) and replaced by 0x88eb28009351fb414a5746f5d8ca91cdc02760d8 on 2024-09-24 at blocks 20820498 (12:36:47Z) and 20820500 (12:37:11Z), constant across 60 samples to the incident. Age from the later of the two installs: 589.5 days rather than 624.2 from deployment

incidents.documentedLastChange: 2024-09-24T12:37:11Z (block 20820500): the RFQ router module slots backing the two exploited selectors were last repointed to 0x88eb28009351fb414a5746f5d8ca91cdc02760d8
